reviewed_changes.source:
Multiple Plotting Areas


PlotJuggler allows you to have multiple Plotting Areas.


- You can split an Area vertically or horizontally (A)

- You may create multiple tabs (B).

- You can temporary see a single Area in "fullscreen" mode (C)

- Areas can be moved and re-arranged. Drag and drop on its title to move it (D)

reviewed_changes.source:
The time tracker


The time tracker is a vertical line that is used to see the value of the curves across Plotting Areas (A). Use button B to customize the amount of information shown.


You can move the time tracker using the time slider at the bottom or pressing [SHIFT + Left Mouse] on any plot.


The purpose of the time tracker is not limited to visualization: in fact, its position triggers the so called "Statepublishers" (C), which will react to the motion of the tracker. Use the play button (D) to animate the tracker.

拖動底部時間滑塊，或在任意繪圖區按Shift + 滑鼠左鍵，即可移動時間遊標。

Apply filters and simple timeseries transforms


PlotJuggler provides an intuitive way to apply transformations to your data using a simple graphical interface. For instance you can apply:


- A moving average filter.

- A first order derivative.

- Calculate the integral.

- An outlier removal.

- Add your own using plugins!

reviewed_changes.source:
Advanced transforms: create a custom timeseries


You can create a Multiple-Inputs / Single Output function using existing timeseries.

The scripting language is based on Lua, a programming language that will take you 5 minutes to understand ;)


A) Main timeseries that provide the time points and a value (mandatory)

B) Additional data source for multi-inputs formulas (optional).

C) The main function called to create a data point.

D) Global context to initialize global variables.

E) Semaphore: red if anything is wrong/missing.

reviewed_changes.source: Save the current function in the library.

Function editor Help


The function editor uses the scrioting language Lua. You may want to read Learn Lua in 15 minutes.


In practice, you don't need to know that much to use it in PlotJuggler.


You should implement the body of a function(time, value), that is invoked for each point. The returned value is the point [time, your_value]


Single input, stateless functions:


Example:


return (value * 2) + 1


or you can use the math library from Lua:


return math.log(value)


The new point will have the same time of the original point. If you want to modify the timestamp, just return two values like this:


return time +1, (value * 2)


Return multiple points at once:


Since version 3.1, you may also return multiple values at once, using a Lua table:


-- Calculate t1,v1, t2, v2, etc...

return { {t1, v1}, {t2, v2} }


Statefull functions:


Some transformations require some form of "memory", i.e. they need the previous value. To do this you may use the "global variable" textbox.


For instance, to compute the finite difference between two consecutive value, you would add this to the Global Variables textbox:


prev = nil


And this to the Function() textbox


if ( prev == nil ) then

prev = value

end


diff = value - prev

prev = value

return diff


Multi input, single output:


Select an additional time series and drop it in the table on the left side. Not your function definition will look like function(time,value,v1)


Average of two time series:


return (value + v1) / 2

reviewed_changes.source:
--[[ Helper function to create a series from arrays


new_series: a series previously created with ScatterXY.new(name)

prefix: prefix of the timeseries, before the index of the array

suffix_X: suffix to complete the name of the series containing the X value. If [nil], use the index of the array.

suffix_Y: suffix to complete the name of the series containing the Y value

timestamp: usually the tracker_time variable

Example:

Assuming we have multiple series in the form:

/trajectory/node.{X}/position/x

/trajectory/node.{X}/position/y

where {N} is the index of the array (integer). We can create a reactive series from the array with:

new_series = ScatterXY.new("my_trajectory")

CreateSeriesFromArray( new_series, "/trajectory/node", "position/x", "position/y", tracker_time );

--]]


function CreateSeriesFromArray( new_series, prefix, suffix_X, suffix_Y, timestamp )

--- clear previous values

new_series:clear()

--- Append points to new_series

index = 0

while(true) do


x = index;

-- if not nil, get the X coordinate from a series

if suffix_X ~= nil then

series_x = TimeseriesView.find( string.format( "%s.%d/%s", prefix, index, suffix_X) )

if series_x == nil then break end

x = series_x:atTime(timestamp)

end

series_y = TimeseriesView.find( string.format( "%s.%d/%s", prefix, index, suffix_Y) )

if series_y == nil then break end

y = series_y:atTime(timestamp)

new_series:push_back(x,y)

index = index+1

end

end


--[[ Similar to the built-in function GetSeriesNames(), but select only the names with a give prefix. --]]


function GetSeriesNamesByPrefix(prefix)

-- GetSeriesNames(9 is a built-in function

all_names = GetSeriesNames()

filtered_names = {}

for i, name in ipairs(all_names) do

-- check the prefix

if name:find(prefix, 1, #prefix) then

table.insert(filtered_names, name);

end

end

return filtered_names

end


--[[ Modify an existing series, applying offsets to all their X and Y values


series: an existing timeseries, obtained with TimeseriesView.find(name)

delta_x: offset to apply to each x value

delta_y: offset to apply to each y value

--]]


function ApplyOffsetInPlace(series, delta_x, delta_y)

-- use C++ indices, not Lua indices

for index=0, series:size()-1 do

x,y = series:at(index)

series:set(index, x + delta_x, y + delta_y)

end

end

index = 0

while(true) do


x = index;

-- 不為 nil 時，從序列取得 X 座標

if suffix_X ~= nil then

series_x = TimeseriesView.find( string.format( "%s.%d/%s", prefix, index, suffix_X) )

if series_x == nil then break end

x = series_x:atTime(timestamp)

end

series_y = TimeseriesView.find( string.format( "%s.%d/%s", prefix, index, suffix_Y) )

if series_y == nil then break end

y = series_y:atTime(timestamp)

new_series:push_back(x,y)

index = index+1

end

end


--[[ 類似內建函式 GetSeriesNames()，但僅選擇具有指定字首的名稱。--]]


function GetSeriesNamesByPrefix(prefix)

-- GetSeriesNames() 是內建函式

all_names = GetSeriesNames()

filtered_names = {}

for i, name in ipairs(all_names) do

-- 檢查字首

if name:find(prefix, 1, #prefix) then

table.insert(filtered_names, name);

end

end

return filtered_names

end


--[[ 修改現有序列，為所有 X 和 Y 值應用偏移量


series：透過 TimeseriesView.find(name) 獲得的現有序列

delta_x：每個 X 值的偏移量

delta_y：每個 Y 值的偏移量

--]]


function ApplyOffsetInPlace(series, delta_x, delta_y)

-- 使用 C++ 索引，而非 Lua 索引

for index=0, series:size()-1 do

x,y = series:at(index)

series:set(index, x + delta_x, y + delta_y)

end

end
